I found a copy of this book on a bus, back in the days before the internet. I started reading it and was hooked. Instead of going to meet my friends, I took the book with me to a coffee shop and spent the night reading it. Next morning, I went down to the bookstore to find out what other books he had written. I still feel let down every time I think about what he could have created.

Ignatius is an incredible character. There should be no reason to like him. No reason to root for him. He's an internet troll in the age before computers. He has no inherent goodness to him. He causes destruction wherever he goes. Yet somehow he resonates. No matter how happy or successful we are, there's a part of us that is a shitty, arrogant, lazy, self absorbed person. Perhaps it's that which makes us feel sympathy for him. By embracing Ignatius, we embrace the worst of ourselves, and find absolution in that act.

Or, navel gazing aside, it's simply a damn funny book.

I have no idea if Confederacy of Dunces is my favorite humorous book or if it's Catch-22, but it's a book I will always re-read.

I read it about 25 years ago and hated it. I was living in New Orleans at the time and it was sort of required reading. Not only did I hate it, I questioned the intelligence of anyone that liked it. For some reason it just irritated me.

A sign of good literature is that it can evoke strong feelings, so it passed that test. My wife bought it for me a few months ago, not knowing that I had already read it. I guess I'll have to re-read it and see if it got any better.

I enjoyed it, but it's a shame it never got the editor it really needed. Cut out one third of the junk, and it would be a comic masterpiece. As it is, it's just a bit too long and a bit too repetitive for me to want to read it a second time.

I read it 25 years ago and hated it (see previous post). Picked it up last night to give it another try. Made it 100 pages before giving up. It's at least as bad as I remember, maybe worse. The only way I can describe it is that it is just plain irritating to read. 100 pages of fingernails on blackboard. Clearly many people like it. Different strokes, I guess.

I learned about voat through a similar site I was a part of for a few years; you've probably never heard of it.

Why I left the other place: I'd first like to say that I'm not trying to put anyone down. For the most part, I loved it there; at first. The information and entertainment at my fingertips seemed endless. However, for some time now, I've noticed that it's grown more and more mundane and hollow (or, maybe I just started seeing what it really was). Recycled posts continually making the front page, regurgitated comments with nothing to add dominating the discussion, and a relative handful of users getting power-hungry and knowingly escalating these issues for the sake of meaningless points. Somehow, the points became the personal goal for a lot of users, where they were originally meant to improve the quality of the site in our favor.

Why I came here: Following a link in a discussion about alternative sites, I saw an opportunity to be a part of what the old stomping ground was meant to be. I've been lurking for a few days now (between down times), and after checking out several subverses in depth, I'm confident that it can be just that. I feel like my opinion will matter here, and will be weighed and measured accordingly, rather than ignored for being original, or shot down for being different.

To clear up any conjecture: I love the ability to speak freely without censorship. I don't hate people who look different. I feel that anyone who is not happy with their bodies should be comfortable with discussing ways to cope, and if they choose, change at a healthy and reasonable pace, without being laughed or scowled at.

Anyway, I'm excited to be a part of what seems to be an overall great and diverse community. Any Good subverses I should know about?
